# This file is generated from dorg-mutate-grammar.el.  Do not edit.
** Semantic mutation grammar

The inventory below is the single semantic source for reference prose, CLI help, and Emacs completion.  The accepted language remains =dorg-api-normalize=; every inventory example is checked against it.

*** Targets and safety

| Target | Cardinality | Missing | Duplicates | Projection | Confirmation |
|--------+-------------+---------+------------+------------+--------------|
| ~(id N)~ | exactly-one | invalid-target | impossible | numeric-heading-id | none |
| ~(key V)~ | exactly-one | invalid-target | identity-violation | exact-source-identity | none |
| ~document~ | exactly-one | impossible | impossible | document-host | none |
| ~(where QUERY)~ | zero-many | empty-selection | deduplicated | policy-key-when-present-else-existing-heading-id | expected targets on apply |

A supplied base revision is checked by CAS; omitting it does not imply a check.  Query-scoped apply requires the exact targets resolved by dry-run. Broad-write confirmation is an independent safety gate.

*** Address-refinement law

Collection address components refine left-to-right.  An =occurrence= selector chooses an element of that collection; a position token chooses an insertion slot.  Arity follows the declared address depth and is never padded with a selector that has no referent.

*** Verb laws

- *set*: Assign an intrinsic slot or upsert a unique addressed cell; it may create the cell when absent.
- *replace-element*: Strictly rewrite an addressed existing occurrence; a missing occurrence is an error.
- *replace-sequence*: Make the complete sequence equal the supplied non-empty sequence; keyword sequences may materialize when absent.
- *insert*: Create one element at an explicit position; drawer-line insertion may create its missing first drawer.
- *delete*: Remove the addressed cell, occurrence, sequence, heading, or subtree.

There is no universal rule that insert is the only creator: property set, keyword-sequence replace, and bounded drawer-line insertion have the creation behavior stated above.

*** Heading fields

Heading fields are intrinsic singleton slots.  Their value domains, clearing assignments, and relational projections are explicit below.

| Field | Value domain | Cardinality | Clearing | Projection |
|-------+--------------+-------------+----------+------------|
| title | string | singleton | empty-string | headings.title |
| todo | token-string-or-nil | singleton | nil-or-empty-string | headings.todo_keyword |
| priority | priority-string-or-nil | singleton | nil | headings.priority |
| tags | tag-list | singleton | empty-list | heading_tags |
| commented | boolean-nil-or-t | singleton | nil | headings.commented |

*** Insert-heading constructor clauses

Constructor clauses initialize one bounded heading subtree in the same mutation. The =commented= clause is an exact singleton boolean; explicit =nil= is a value, not omission.  Empty =items= and =children= clauses likewise remain explicit empty singleton values.  Literal descendants are finite constructor payload, not expanded targets: their created-set size does not feed =dorg-api-broad-write-threshold=; the resolved target count remains independently gated.

| Clause | Value domain | Cardinality | IR field | Projection |
|--------+--------------+-------------+----------+------------|
| title | string-or-nil | singleton | title | headings.title |
| todo | token-string-or-nil | singleton | todo | headings.todo_keyword |
| priority | priority-string-or-nil | singleton | priority | headings.priority |
| tags | tag-list | singleton | tags | heading_tags |
| property | property-key-and-string | repeatable | items | property_entries |
| commented | boolean-nil-or-t | singleton | commented | headings.commented |
| items | ordered-item-forms | singleton | items | heading-items |
| children | recursive-heading-constructors | singleton | children | headings |

*** Clearing law

Clearing is defined per exposed target kind, with one canonical spelling for each supported intent.

| Kind | Clearing | Canonical spelling |
|------+----------+--------------------|
| property | delete | ~(delete (property KEY))~ |
| keyword-occurrence | delete | ~(delete (keyword KEY (occurrence N)))~ |
| keyword-sequence | delete | ~(delete (keywords KEY))~ |
| heading | empty-assignment | ~documented nil, empty string, or empty list by FIELD~ |
| planning | empty-assignment | ~nil~ |
| items | unsupported-public | ~no public clear; replace requires at least one item~ |
| text | unsupported-public | ~no public clear~ |
| drawer-line | unsupported-public | ~no public clear~ |

The full items replacement is a broad hammer: it assigns the complete ordered item sequence and requires at least one item.  The public grammar has no clear-items operation.
